To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we developed a mapping framework able, to extract structured knowledge representations from text, to reason with uncertainty in the mapping process, and to learn from a limited amount knowledge sources, which can be used in the context of games.

(1) the use of a constrained learning algorithm for the mapping from natural language to a structured representation of the story, (2) the use of genetic algorithms for solving the structured classification problem, and (3) the use of an ensemble of classifiers, are all important factors for the performance of our system.

we developed a novel mapping framework for extracting actions and their attributes from narrative text that outperforms the state of the art, and we introduced a new constrained Bayesian network learning algorithm that improves the generalization capacity of the mapping framework while reducing the amount of annotated data needed to train it.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the mapping of natural-language sentences in written stories into a structured knowledge representation, i.e., a set of action instances, each one representing an event that took place in a given story.
the development of novel algorithms and techniques to improve the automatic mapping of written narratives to structured knowledge representations.

the development of a mapping framework able of learning to map natural language sentences to a structured knowledge representations, and of exploiting external resources to improve the quality of the resulting interpretations.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the proposed approach outperforms the baseline algorithm in all cases, except in one of the experiments, which is due to the lack of data for learning the mapping.
the proposed mapping framework is able to exploit efficiently the state-of-the- art resources in natural language and knowledge representations to yield a structured interpretation of sentences.
the proposed approach yields an efficient solution for a structured classification problem with an exponential number of possible instance combinations.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we propose an efficient algorithm for mapping sentences in a story to a structured knowledge representations, and that the algorithm can be applied in game construction to reduce the knowledge acquisition bottleneck.

the proposed mapping framework, which combines a novel genetic algorithm with the constrained learning algorithm, yields performance gains in mapping sentences from a narrative text to a structured knowledge base, when compared with a state-of-the-art baseline algorithm.

the mapping of natural-language sentences to a knowledge representation can be seen as a structured classification problem, which can be efficiently approached by the proposed algorithm, which is based on a novel formulation of a genetic-algorithm, and which is able to reason with evidence from external sources.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, even with a limited amount of data, it is possible to learn to map natural language sentences to a structured representation of actions and entities.

a novel mapping algorithm for structured knowledge representation can improve the performance in mapping sentences from a story to a knowledge base, which in turn may improve the performance of game construction systems.

the proposed mapping framework is able to exploit external resources to improve the generalization of the system, while being able to learn from a limited amount (in the order of 10 sentences) of labeled data.
